paper.title_en: Coulomb scaling, geometric normalization, and the limits of a single-Gaussian description of sub-barrier fusion across seven projectile species
paper.abstract_en: We analyze 67 heavy-ion fusion reactions with high-quality sub-barrier excitation functions using the single-Gaussian model of Jiang et al. [Phys. Rev. C 112, 034612 (2025)] and extract the barrier parameters <math><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></math>. The reactions involve seven projectiles, <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Si</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>28</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>34</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math>, and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>40</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, on targets from <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts></math> to <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Pb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>208</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The mean barrier height <math><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></math> scales linearly with <math><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> (<math><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.999</mn></mrow></math>), while <math><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></math> correlates strongly with <math><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></math> (<math><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow></math>). The <math><mi>η</mi></math> dependence accounts for 45% of the variation in fusion strength. After removing this geometric dependence, the resulting structure ratio <math><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>η</mi></msub></math> shows no correlation with static target deformation or neutron-transfer <math><mi>Q</mi></math> value. For the 24 systems with at least one open transfer channel, however, <math><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>η</mi></msub></math> correlates strongly with an effective transfer coupling strength <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi></math> (<math><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.70</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>), whereas the <math><mi>Q</mi></math> value alone does not. Thus, positive-transfer <math><mi>Q</mi></math> values are necessary but not sufficient for fusion enhancement, with the transfer coupling strength playing a key role. Systems showing the largest deviations from the geometric trend provide promising candidates for detailed coupled-channels studies.
